structured_output.summary:
Main finding: almost every accuracy conclusion since E021 rests on single 3-seed draws inside the ~0.2-0.33 pp config-to-config noise. The process is also compounding selection bias. Cuts were kept on draws that cleared 0.753 by a hair. Salt-1 companions were run only after those keeps, so they came in lower by regression to the mean, which the loop misread as 'favourable official seeds'.

Two factual problems need checking first. (1) The E043 post-mortem blames max-autotune for the loss of determinism, but E018 and E020 smoke tests, both after max-autotune was enabled, matched their official runs exactly. Whether the noise comes from salts or from run-to-run nondeterminism is unknown, and one identical re-run would settle it. (2) E027's description says it re-ran E021, but its outcome calls it E025. The pooled 0.7533 estimate that all later bars use depends on which one it was.

Most wasteful decision: E042 (pooling swap, -0.19 s, identical forward and backward apart from ties) was discarded because the accuracy re-rolled. Numerically equivalent cuts should be judged on time alone.

On the hypotheses: H6 (accuracy capped by capacity) and the 'epochs no longer help' story rest on two confounded single draws (E032, E036). The clean anchor-fixed slope test, which H6's own falsification criterion requires, was never run. The pp/s exchange rate used to score every cut was measured on SGD and a pre-resizing net, and may now be close to 0. H1.3.1 (E012) and H4.2 (E019) are overclaimed, and H1.5 cites unrelated evidence.

Untested directions: alternating flip, weight decay, the BN-bias LR, the whitening-bias window between 8 steps and 3 epochs, cheaper capacity (group 3 at 640, group-2 width), cutting group 2 to 2 convs, freezing at 28 px, and the free RULES.md check for H5.

Recommended path: (a) identical re-run to fix the noise model; (b) a second draw of E024 to find where the margin went; (c) the anchor-fixed epoch-slope test; (d) one margin source verified with 2 draws, then all banked time cuts stacked in a single run.
